san-ho-won-san-francisco-ca.text: San Ho Won is Benu chef Corey Lee and Jeong-In Hwang's Michelin-starred take on Korean charcoal barbecue — a casual-feeling Mission District room that refuses shortcuts. The duo, both fine-dining-trained under the likes of Guy Savoy, Marco Pierre White and Thomas Keller, grill premium, precisely butchered cuts over lychee-wood charcoal made specially for the restaurant, alongside home-style dishes like pork jowl and an aged kimchi jjigae with soy-cured ramp. Depth and purity of flavor in a relaxed KBBQ setting.

selby-s-atherton-ca.text: Selby's is a glamorous, 10,000-square-foot Silicon Valley grand room near Atherton from the Bacchus Management Group (Spruce, The Village Pub), overseen by two-Michelin-star chef Mark Sullivan. The Michelin-starred kitchen delivers modern takes on classic American cuisine, boosted by produce from the group's private SMIP Ranch: a fresh-baked Gruyère popover, butter-poached Maine lobster with gnocchi and black trumpets, hand-shaped tortellini of slow-cooked duck. It is backed by one of the country's largest cellars, up to 40,000 bottles.

seline-santa-monica-ca.text: Seline is Dave Beran's intimate Santa Monica room, opened in December 2024 and awarded a Michelin star in 2026 — the same year Beran won the James Beard Best Chef: California award. Designed to dissolve the barrier between diners and kitchen, it serves a personal, high-concept tasting of 14 to 17 courses (around $295) that meditates on themes like the progression of the seasons, full of surprises, including ice cream dropped mid-savory. Deeply personal, produce-driven Southern California cooking.

shin-sushi-encino-ca.text: Shin Sushi is Taketoshi Azumi's eight-seat Encino omakase, named for his late father's Tokyo restaurant — a sign from which hangs behind the counter. An Asanebo and Mori Sushi veteran with two decades of experience and a family sushi heritage, Azumi serves the most literal form of omakase: you eat what you're handed until full, and only then does the bill appear. Michelin-starred, it is authentic Edomae sushi — 12 to 14 pieces of meticulously sourced nigiri, tradition front and center.

silvers-omakase-santa-barbara-ca.text: In Santa Barbara's Funk Zone, Silvers Omakase is chef Lennon Silvers Lee's ten-seat sushi room, Michelin-starred within a year of opening. Its two-hour, 13-to-20-course Edomae tasting, roughly three-quarters sushi, uses house-milled Japanese rice and locally and Japan-sourced fish, often dry-aged, plated on handcrafted Yu Maruta ceramics and Kagami crystal. As much a showcase for its community of sake brewers, glassblowers and potters as for Lee's precise craft.

six-test-kitchen-paso-robles-ca.text: Six Test Kitchen began in 2015 as a six-seat counter in Ricky Odbert's father's garage and grew into San Luis Obispo County's first Michelin star — now a twelve-seat, open-kitchen stage in Paso Robles' Tin City. Odbert's constantly evolving, sometimes nightly-changing tasting distills the Central Coast from trusted farmers, foragers and fishermen: dill meringue with trout roe, aged pork loin with burnt-onion purée, barley-koji ice cream with whipped miso. A hyper-seasonal work perpetually in progress.

soichi-san-diego-ca.text: Soichi is chef Soichi Kadoya's intimate University Heights omakase in San Diego, run with his wife Raechel and family — Michelin-starred since 2021. A purist with a nearly three-decade career, and a former fixture at Sushi Tadokoro, Kadoya honors sushi tradition and a low-waste ethos that uses nearly every part of the fish: Hokkaido pike mackerel with ginger and scallion, twice-miso-marinated broiled sea bass, triggerfish nigiri crowned with its own creamy liver. Deliberately small, and determined to stay that way.

sorrel-san-francisco-ca.text: Sorrel is Alex Hong's Cal-Italian restaurant in Pacific Heights, Michelin-starred since 2019 — a refined-yet-approachable room where a rooftop garden supplies herbs, flowers and vegetables. A Quince alum, Hong has a gift for pasta: smoky potato žlikrofi with plum mostarda and horseradish, strascinati in an 'nduja sauce with butter beans and lovage, ricotta gnudi with fried sage and sour cherry. Seasonal California ingredients through an Italian lens, simply and precisely handled.

ssal-san-francisco-ca.text: Ssal is Junsoo and Hyunyoung Bae's Korean tasting-menu restaurant on Polk Street — opened in 2019 with their wedding-gift money and no outside investors, reborn in 2021 as a minimalist fine-dining room. Chef Junsoo Bae, a CIA grad who cooked at Noma and Per Se, blends French training with Korean flavors and won a Michelin star in 2022: a golden sweet-potato pancake with Kaluga caviar, a soondubu riff of silken tofu with octopus, mussels and crab-laced miso. Refined simplicity, deeply personal.

state-bird-provisions-san-francisco-ca.text: State Bird Provisions is Stuart Brioza and Nicole Krasinski's genre-bending Fillmore restaurant — "dim sum and a great hors d'oeuvre party morphed into one experience," as Krasinski puts it. Michelin-starred since 2013 and a James Beard winner, it sends finely crafted small dishes around on dim-sum carts: potato chips with crème fraîche and cured trout roe, savory chanterelle pancakes with lardo, and its namesake signature — fried quail, California's state bird, with stewed onions. Playful, inventive and beloved.

ariete-miami-fl.text: In a lush, greenery-filled Coconut Grove room, Ariete is Michael Beltran's Cuban-American love letter to Miami — classic French technique married to his Cuban heritage and local ingredients, Michelin-starred since 2022. The menu reimagines the familiar: fluke with conch escabeche, fish chorizo and tomato ragout; venison tartare with bone-marrow sabayon; the Cuban sandwich remade as a delicate pithivier; a dramatic tableside duck press. Rooted in Miami, refined through the classics.

boia-de-miami-fl.text: Boia De is Luciana Giangrandi and Alex Meyer's buzzy neighborhood boîte in a Miami strip mall — a modern-American, Italian-leaning room the chef couple grew into one of Miami's first Michelin stars in 2022. Alumni of The NoMad, Carbone and Eleven Madison Park, they cook crispy polenta with marinated eggplant and ricotta salata, handmade pastas like rabbit-and-rosemary pappardelle and Alba-truffle tagliatelle, and veal sweetbreads with beets and jalapeño. Small, brilliant and unpretentious.

camille-orlando-fl.text: Camille made history as the first Vietnamese restaurant in the U.S. to earn a Michelin star — a French-Vietnamese room in Orlando's Baldwin Park from Vietnamese-born chef Tung Phan. Trained at Le Cordon Bleu, Phan uses French technique to honor Vietnamese flavors and memory across a ten-course tasting: pho reimagined as a cloud-like aromatic foam, a Dungeness crab curry tartlet, sweet-potato brioche with "gold" chocolate ice cream and Vietnamese-coffee sauce. Refined, inventive and personal.

chef-s-counter-at-maass-fort-lauderdale-.text: Chef's Counter at MAASS is Ryan Ratino's Fort Lauderdale outpost — the D.C. chef behind Bresca and two-star Jônt — a fourteen-seat perch facing the open kitchen at the Four Seasons. Michelin-starred and executed nightly by chef David Brito, the tasting menu blends French technique, Japanese ingredients and Florida highlights into an elegant, big-city experience with a playful streak. Precise, seasonal and a little bit fun.

cote-miami-miami-fl.text: Cote Miami brought Simon Kim's Michelin-starred "Korean Steakhouse" concept to the Design District in 2021 — Korean barbecue's fire fused with the regal American steakhouse. Beyond tableside smokeless grills and a Butcher's Feast, its ten-course Steak Omakase runs through Miyazaki A5 wagyu and Ossetra caviar, backed by a red-lit dry-aging room, a vegetable-fermentation lab and a signature three-salt blend. The Miami sibling to Kim's original New York Cote.

ebbe-tampa-fl.text: Ebbe is chef Ebbe Vollmer's hyper-focused downtown Tampa counter — a sleek, U-shaped marble bar serving a single, ever-changing tasting menu that runs "from fantastic Florida to essential Scandinavia." Michelin-starred, it weaves the Swedish chef's roots through local produce and European specialties: a beet roulade in brown-butter and black-cherry sauce, turbot with fermented white asparagus and sturgeon caviar, braised oxtail with seared foie gras. Chef-driven and passion-fueled.

elcielo-miami-miami-fl.text: Elcielo is Colombian chef Juan Manuel Barrientos's Michelin-starred, multisensory journey through the flavors and rituals of Colombia — a Brickell tasting-menu room near the Miami River. Across some eighteen courses, ancestral Colombian cooking meets avant-garde technique and Florida ingredients, from a Salpicón-punch welcome to the signature "Chocotherapy" ritual guests remember most. Barrientos cares as much about how the food makes you feel as how it tastes.

emelina-west-palm-beach-fl.text: Emelina made history as the first Cuban restaurant in North America to earn a Michelin star — a sixteen-seat West Palm Beach tasting room that took its star less than four months after its 2026 debut. Husband-and-wife chefs Osmel González and Camila Salazar don't reproduce familiar Cuban dishes; they speculate on what Cuban cuisine might have become without decades of isolation: poached local oysters with yucca foam, dry-aged beef with green-mango mojo and black-bean sauce, a reimagined rabo encendido. Heritage through imagination.

hiden-miami-fl.text: Hiden lives up to its name — an eight-seat "secret room" omakase hidden behind a code-locked door at the back of a Wynwood taco shop, reached only with a passcode emailed hours before dinner. Chef Seijun Okano serves a constantly changing, 16-to-18-course tasting built on seasonal ingredients and raw fish flown from Japan. Michelin-starred, with a months-long waitlist — one of Miami's most coveted, and most clandestine, tables.

kadence-orlando-fl.text: Kadence is Orlando's omakase benchmark — an eight-seat, unmarked black box in Audubon Park where husband-and-wife chefs Mark Berdin and Jennifer Bañagale serve traditional Edomae sushi, Michelin-starred five years running. Grown from their East End Market stand Kappo, the minimalist counter focuses entirely on technique, sourcing and ingredient quality across a roughly $311 prepaid tasting. Speakeasy in feel, exacting in craft.

koya-tampa-fl.text: Koya was Tampa's first omakase-only destination and among the first three Tampa restaurants to earn a Michelin star in 2023 — an eight-seat Hyde Park counter from Eric and Adriana Fralick. Chef Eric Fralick's "singular interpretation of Japanese cuisine," built on seasonal ingredients flown in from Japan, earned a James Beard Best New Restaurant nod. Minimalist, leisurely-paced and deeply personal.

kosen-tampa-fl.text: Kōsen — "ray of light" — is a Michelin-starred Tampa Heights omakase from the Omei Restaurant Group's Tung brothers, led by executive chef Andrew Huang. Its ten-seat counter runs a 20-plus-course omakase, with kaiseki menus in the dining room besides, blending tradition and innovation, sourcing from local regenerative farmers and running an in-house fermentation program that eliminates single-use plastics. Brilliant, sustainable and immersive.
